Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week. Mon Laferte to Receive Social Justice Award This week, it was announced that Mon Laferte will receive the Social Justice Award at the 39th annual Hispanic Heritage Awards, taking place Sept. 10 at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis. The Chilean singer will be honored for using her art, music and platforms to promote conversations about human rights, gender equality and social justice in Latin America and around the world. “I feel incredibly honored. I never imagined that a moment would come in my life or career when my work to carry out the projects that truly matter to me would be recognized,” Laferte said in a statement. “I believe one of the greatest strengths of the Latino community is our ability to build connections, welcome and care for one another, wherever we may be. title: Vera Blue covers Radiohead’s ‘Creep’ for triple j’s Like A Version
summary: Blue also performed "Maze," a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals.
body: Vera Blue has taken on one of alternative rock’s most enduring songs, covering Radiohead ‘s “Creep” for triple j’s Like A Version . The Australian singer-songwriter stripped the 1992 track back to three elements — electric guitar, piano and vocals — building from the lower end of her range into a soaring falsetto by the chorus. Late in the performance she deployed The Pipe, a mouth-controlled dynamic effects processor and synthesizer made by SOMA Laboratory, adding an eerie texture to the arrangement. Blue said she was drawn to the song’s emotional core, describing “Creep” as an “epic rock song” whose lyrics are also “heartbreaking,” and aiming for a “very haunting version” that still nods to Thom Yorke’s original. Blue also performed “Maze,” a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals , during her studio session. The album is due Friday, Aug. 21 via Island Records/Universal Music Australia, and Blue will support it with a national tour opening the same night at Brisbane’s Princess Theatre and running through Perth’s The Rechabite on Aug. 28. Born Celia Pavey, Ve…

title: Brandi Carlile Postpones U.K. and European Tour Citing ‘Personal Circumstances’
summary: The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027.
body: Brandi Carlile has postponed the UK and European leg of her tour, citing “personal circumstances,” the singer-songwriter announced on social media Friday (Aug. 7). The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027. Carlile did not specify the reason beyond describing it as a personal matter. View this post on Instagram “I have been so profoundly anxious about this decision, and I’m aware that this change may be disappointing and inconvenient for many of you, especially those of you who were planning on traveling internationally,” she wrote, adding that she hoped the rescheduling would give fans time to adjust their plans. “I want nothing more than to see my friends across the pond and I have done everything in my power to avoid rescheduling this tour.” The postponement affects several dates. Carlile’s Lisbon show has been canceled outright, while two new dates in Wolverhampton, England, and Copenhagen have been added. summary: Worsham issues his first independent album, Once Upon a Second Time Around, and discusses his multifaceted career.
body: Two decades after studying at Boston’s Berklee College of Music and relocating to Nashville, Mississippi native Charlie Worsham has forged a career as an award-winning artist/songwriter/musician. He’s a multi-hyphenate artist in his own right, but is also a first-call session player, touring bandmate, and essential thread in the fabric of country music’s current landscape. His new album, Once Upon a Second Time Around , out Friday (Aug. 7), is his third full-length solo project, following 2013’s Rubberband and 2017’s The Beginning of Things , as well as the 2023 EP Compadres , but also launches a new independent era: The album is out on ONErpm after he spent years with Warner Records Nashville. Concurrently with releasing his own music, Worsham has lent his prowess on guitar, mandolin, banjo and songwriting to albums by Eric Church, Carrie Underwood, Ella Langley, Kacey Musgraves, Kip Moore, Sam Williams, Luke Combs, and Dierks Bentley. He’s been part of touring bands for Vince Gill and Bentley, as well as briefly joining Old Crow Medicine Show.
